AD AGENTS before AD AGENCY

ERROR before CURSE for the bad spelling  ("Confirmed" by the 2nd R)

UNWISE before UNWARY for incautious.

NOODLE before NOOGIE for "annoying knuckling"  What do I know about these frat-boy practices?  Or maybe it's sixth grade?

The clue would have to read "Find a spot for on, as a schedule," though that's incredibly clunky.

I was with you until you got to “who let this puzzle get approved”; before you make a statement like that, read other comments and consider whether you are missing anything. In this case, when people are flummoxed by a theme I suggest they step back and look at the bigger picture. 

“Periwinkle” is meant to indicate EYESOFBLUE; surely no one has periwinkle eyes, it’s just a type of blue, and the “eyes” come from the letter I. Sure, maybe it’s not the most common color, but the constructor needed one that had multiple I’s; and it’s not uncommon, and if you haven’t heard of it, it should have become obvious at that point. 

And then look at the other themers and see how they compare. So, PEASINAPOD in not a synonym for “Group of Porpoises”, that’s just the POD part, so it’s consistent.

As for EYESOFBLUE, maybe it is generational; not that I was around in ‘20s when this song was written, but it certainly is familiar to me:

Five foot two, eyes of blue,
But oh! what those five foot could do,
Has anybody seen my gal?

None the less, “eyes of blue” is a perfectly cromulent idiom whether you are familiar with it or not and a fair compromise for the theme set.

So, I understand this frustrated you and why, sorry you had that experience; but there was nothing in this puzzle that should have precluded its approval, quite the contrary if you consider the abundant praise in other comments.
